meeting_header:
Date: 2025-11-12 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Avery Lin (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Kaur (Redwood CSM); Maya Patel (Arcadia Head of ML), Evan Chu (Arcadia SRE), Liam O'Neal (Arcadia Product), Sofia Martinez (Arcadia Data Eng)
summary: Weekly pilot sync focused on quality evaluation, recent regressions, and failure-mode triage for Arcadia's sensor-data summarization pilot. SE presented preliminary scoring distribution changes after moving to a fused-attn quantized variant; customer shared two high-severity regressions and network-related throttling concerns. Agreed next steps include focused benchmarks, prompt set upload, and security docs exchange.
topics: Quality trend: aggregated score shifts vs baseline
Infrastructure: KV cache, batching, and egress
Pilot economics: cost vs latency tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Avery Lin: Okay, hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is the weekly Arcadia pilot health check. We got about 42 minutes, we'll run through the scorecard, the two regressions you flagged, then action items.
[00:12] Maya Patel: Yep, thanks. We have limited time so I'll jump in—last week we onboarded the quantized-fused variant and saw a change in meat of outputs, some cases were fine, two were pretty bad.
[00:28] Diego Ramos: Right, Diego from Redwood, SE. I pulled the comparative histograms; overall token latency dropped, cost per token down roughly 28% in our microbench, but there's a tail in the confidence scores for long-context summaries.
[00:42] Liam O'Neal: By tail you mean accuracy tail—where it messes up on long event sequences?
[00:50] Diego Ramos: Exactly, the model is OK up to about 1.5k context, after that the fused quant path seems to drop some cross-attention fidelity in our profiling. Could be kernel approximations in the fused attention implementation.
[01:05] Maya Patel: We saw two concrete failures: one where the summary omitted a critical alert (false negative) and one hallucinated a nonexistent calibration value. Both are bad for incident triage.
[01:17] Sofia Martinez: And to add, our SREs observed intermittent 503s during bursts which may coincide with cache eviction storms—we're wondering if batching/auto-scale configuration is interacting badly.
[01:29] Evan Chu: Yeah, on our side, the egress limits in our cloud account also caused throttling when the pilot burst hit peak sensor windows. That makes the perceived latency worse even if tokens are cheaper.
[01:41] Priya Kaur: Priya here; quick housekeeping: we've uploaded the weekly scorecard and the guardrail rule set to the pilot folder (link in the chat). Also, we'll need the 2k prompt set Maya mentioned so the evaluation harness can run deterministically.
[01:55] Avery Lin: Cool. Diego, can you walk through the scoring delta and where the regressions show up on the heatmap?
[02:02] Diego Ramos: Sure. So slide deck GH—sorry, the deck in the drive—shows a shift in F1-like heuristics for entity extraction from 0.92 down to ~0.86 on long-context buckets. The majority of short-context prompts are stable. If you look at the top-right cell of the heatmap, that's where both regressions live.
[02:23] Maya Patel: And those two regressions are reproducible in our test harness, which is why we flagged them. One is prompt ID sensor-01984, the missing alert; the other is sensor-02203, the hallucinated calibration.
[02:36] Diego Ramos: Got it. Two likely hypotheses: (A) quantized kernel math introduced minor rounding leading to borderline token predictions for rare tokens (calibration strings often have low occurrence); (B) caching/prefetching means the key/values are stale on long sequences if eviction policy is aggressive.
[02:55] Evan Chu: Hmm, eviction policy—Sofia, do we have logs for cache hit ratios during the incident windows?
[03:02] Sofia Martinez: We do, not yet uploaded, we'll add them to the shared folder. Early glance shows spike in cache misses exactly when bursts happen.
[03:09] Avery Lin: Ok that suggests an infra component. Diego, can you run a KV-cache stress test that simulates Arcadia's burst patterns? That'll help isolate infra vs model.
[03:18] Diego Ramos: Yes, will do. I'll run a stress harness with the same sequence lengths and concurrency you reported. Also, I'll enable a trace to see if the fused-attn path is dropping context windows.
[03:30] Liam O'Neal: Quick question on guardrails—can we keep the hallucination detector thresholds lower for sensor calibration values? We need strict conservatism on numeric outputs.
[03:37] Diego Ramos: Yes, you can add post-processing guardrails: numeric regex checks + source-of-truth verification. We can also add a policy to fallback to the baseline non-quantized model on numeric-critical prompts.
[03:47] Maya Patel: Fallback sounds sensible but costs are a concern. What's the delta if we route numeric-critical prompts to the non-quantized variant?
[03:55] Diego Ramos: Based on our early numbers, those calls would be roughly 1.6x the token cost but latency increases 20-30%—still under your contained SLO in most cases, but we'll run dedicated benchmarks.
[04:08] Priya Kaur: I'll add a routing policy to the pilot config: a label for critical prompts that forces the baseline variant. AE will capture pricing.
[04:16] Avery Lin: On pricing—I'll update the pilot SOW to include a burst-capacity option and explicit per-variant pricing for the fallback, sent by EOD Friday.
[04:24] Evan Chu: Back to infra: we definitely want Redwood Private on the table because of our egress constraints and KMS/HSM needs for sensor data. Can we do an on-prem demo for our security team?
[04:34] Diego Ramos: Absolutely, we can schedule a Redwood Private demo. It'll cover VPC peering, KMS integration patterns, and audit logs. We'll need a week to provision a demo environment if you want a hands-on test.
[04:46] Maya Patel: That works. Also, for the two failure cases I can share exact logs and expected references.
[04:52] Sofia Martinez: I'll drop the cache hit/miss logs and a timeline mapping to the two incidents into the folder after this call.
[04:58] Diego Ramos: Great. One more technical note: there is a subtle tokenization mismatch on sensor IDs where punctuation handling differs between our tokenizer and your ingestion preprocessor. That can explain omission of short alphanumeric IDs in summaries.
[05:12] Liam O'Neal: Ugh, that rings a bell—our preprocessor strips leading zeros, which would change tokenization. We'll freeze the ingest pipeline for the test run.
[05:20] Avery Lin: Nice catch. Diego, add tokenization alignment to action items.
[05:24] Diego Ramos: Added. Also, I'll run A/B microbench where we 1) keep baseline tokenizer and 2) apply Arcadia's current preprocessor to replicate the failure.
[05:35] Maya Patel: Anything else on scoring? We also wanted to compare precision vs recall tradeoffs—some downstream tools care more about false positives.
[05:43] Diego Ramos: We can generate precision/recall curves on the 2k prompt set once you upload. If you care more about precision, we can shift decoding temperature and apply conservative beam constraints or forced-verbatim rules for device IDs.
[05:56] Priya Kaur: I'm noting next steps: SOW update, prompt upload, KV stress test, cache logs, Redwood Private demo request.
[06:04] Avery Lin: Ok, let's recap responsibilities and deadlines.
[06:08] Maya Patel: To recap from Arcadia: we'll upload prompts and logs; we'll freeze preprocessor for test; security team will review Redwood Private demo invite.
[06:18] Evan Chu: On our end, we'll add VPC egress policy docs and timeline for review.
[06:23] Avery Lin: Redwood: Diego runs cache and tokenizer A/B tests; Diego to run quant vs non-quant fallback benchmarks; Priya to send SOC2/KMS summary; AE to share SOW pricing.
[06:36] Diego Ramos: One small FYI: we briefly considered Replicate as a short-term host for some heavier non-quant calls but given the orchestration/rollout complexity it's not ideal; we can discuss if you want a multi-vendor fallback later.
[06:51] Maya Patel: Noted. For now we want one consistent runtime.
[06:56] Avery Lin: Great. We'll follow up in the shared thread with links. Thanks everyone, we'll reconvene same time next week unless earlier needed.
[07:04] Liam O'Neal: Thanks all.
[07:06] [call ends]
